title: Measurement to Decision Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: A three-layer directed graph of seven measurements, ten derived quantities and fifteen real-world decisions, with downstream and upstream highlighting, a chapter filter, and a sensor-failure mode that counts which decisions become impossible.

learningObjectives: Organise the relationships between measured quantities and the decisions they drive.
Trace any decision back to the measurements it requires.
Identify which decisions depend on more than one quantity.
Judge which measurement matters most for a given decision.
prerequisites: Chapters 5 to 11, which introduce the seven measurements

keyQuestions: How many decisions does one measurement reach?
Which decisions need more than one measurement?
What stops working if this sensor fails?
What does this station not measure that these decisions need?
commonMisconceptions: Each measurement supports one kind of decision.
A single measurement is enough to support a consequential decision.
Every sensor on the station is equally important.
A station measures everything a decision needs.
assessmentOpportunities: Lists every measurement a named decision requires.
Ranks the seven sensors by how many decisions fail without each.
Names the decisions with inputs the station cannot supply.
